feature: Feature 3 — Creating coins: the mint flow, the auto-namer, and the anti-duplicate check

problems.problem: E5 REINTRODUCES $KANG THROUGH THE FRONT DOOR. A5 builds a six-rule substring gate so 'a $KANG-class hallucination is structurally impossible', and A1 caps `llm_prior` at weight 0.35 with 'never primary without corroboration'. Then E5 says the search row's `prefill_symbol` 'wins over the namer's #1'. Trace where that symbol comes from: the 'no coin yet' row is derived from `stories where confirmed_count=0`, and the ticker it displays comes from `narrative_tickers` rows — which per §5.4 and the dataContract include `source='llm'`, i.e. SUGGESTED. So an uncorroborated LLM-invented ticker is injected straight into the primary field, bypassing A5 entirely, and `.namer-why` then reads 'you picked this from search' — laundering model output as user intent. The gate is applied to the model's output and not to the input that overrides it.
problems.fix: Run A5 rules 1, 2, 4, 6 against `prefill_symbol` before it touches the field, exactly as if the model had emitted it. If it fails rule 1 (not a substring of the corpus), do not prefill — put it in `.alts` slot 3 labelled `suggested, not found in the posts`. Additionally: only surface `prefill_symbol` from rows where `narrative_tickers.source IN ('cashtag','mint_in_post')`, never `'llm'`. And `.namer-why` must never say 'you picked this' for a symbol the user did not type — say `from the cashtag in the post` or nothing.

problems.problem: D-STRONG RENDERS BUY ON A MATCH THE MATCHER REFUSED TO CONFIRM. THE ONE RULE says the primary is a pure function of CONFIRMED count. B2's D-STRONG band flips the primary to `Buy $FERRY` on a heuristic the matcher never ran: exact symbol + `first_mint_at >= earliest_post_at - 10min` + liquidity >= $1k + (pHash<=6 OR name-cos>=0.75). By construction this band only fires on coins the matcher did NOT confirm — if it had, the form would not have opened (D-CONFIRMED). So the create flow ships a second, looser, undocumented matcher, and the loose one gets the Buy button that §5.9 and D1 explicitly withhold. Worse, B3 correctly identifies the denial-of-creation attack for UNSURE, then builds a band that is strictly easier to attack and pays the attacker: mint $FERRY with the post's image inside the window, seed $1k, and Insidor points every would-be creator at your coin with a primary Buy.
problems.fix: Delete the primary-button flip from D-STRONG. Keep everything else in the band — the `.dupe-card`, the amber `.coll.taken`, the `You'd be the second $FERRY. The first has $18.2K in it.` cost line, and a bordered secondary `Buy $FERRY`. Primary stays `Review $TICKER`. If the evidence really is strong enough to sell a Buy, it is strong enough to feed the matcher: post the D-STRONG feature vector to the §5.6 scorer and let it return CONFIRMED, at which point D-CONFIRMED handles it through the one sanctioned path. One matcher, one threshold, one Buy button.

problems.problem: NO STATE FOR TWO COINS LANDING DURING THE FORM. The duplicate interstitial is single-coin by construction: headline `$FERRY was made 40 seconds ago.`, one `.dupe-card`, primary `Buy $FERRY`. On a hot story the modal case is a copycat swarm — §5.2 names same-ticker swarms as the one thing that degrades the temporal gate, and the 40-second open-to-sign window on the hottest story is exactly where two mints land. When it happens the spec renders a Buy pointing at whichever row sorted first, which is the 'buy which one?' ambiguity THE ONE RULE exists to forbid, rendered at the moment the user is holding a signature.
problems.fix: Add a fourth interstitial state keyed on `count(new CONFIRMED) >= 2`: headline `Two $FERRY coins were made while you were here.`, both `.dupe-card`s stacked with liquidity/holders/age, primary `See the 2 coins` (matching THE ONE RULE's >=2 branch), secondary `Make a different one`, tertiary `Show me the story`. Same rule on E7: with `confirmed_count >= 2` the pre-expanded D-STRONG panel must list all of them, not 'the existing coin'.

problems.problem: THE CENTRAL JUSTIFICATION NUMBER IS INVERTED, AND `can_create` IS UNDEFINED. The summary claims create is the landing state '50-70% of the time by story coinability (§3.5)'. §3.5 says the opposite: 'Expect 50-70% of promoted stories to come back `coinable: false`, rendered with no CTA.' The spec has read a suppression rate as a create rate — a 2x error in the sizing of the feature it exists to justify. Downstream this is a real gap, not just rhetoric: §3.5's `coinable` boolean includes `normalizeTickers(ticker_candidates).length > 0`, and the dataContract adds `coinability_tier`, `coinable` AND `sensitive` as three separate columns without ever defining how `story_cta_v.can_create` combines them. If `can_create = tier >= 2` only, the Create CTA renders on the 50-70% of stories §3.5 says must have none. If it is `tier >= 2 AND coinable`, then A8's third row (`namable=false` on an otherwise normal story → 'the form opens anyway') is unreachable dead UI, because a story with no ticker candidates already failed `coinable`.
problems.fix: Write the definition into the spec: `can_create = coinability_tier = 2 AND coinable = true AND NOT sensitive`. Then either delete A8 row 3 as unreachable, or explicitly decouple `coinable` (a naming-quality judgement that should NOT gate the CTA) from `coinability_tier` (a harm judgement that must), and drop `normalizeTickers(...) > 0` from the §3.5 `coinable` formula — a story with no ticker candidate is precisely what the A1 harvester exists to fix and should not be pre-suppressed by the model. Restate the summary's sizing with the corrected number.

problems.problem: THE PRE-SIGN RE-CHECK IS STRUCTURALLY BLIND TO THE WINDOW IT EXISTS FOR. Its stated job is to catch a mint in the last ~40 seconds. B4 says that when `coin_index` is stale it 'bypasses the index entirely, going direct to Jupiter/DexScreener'. But the spec's own success screen states there is no DexScreener pair and no Jupiter price for 60-90s after launch, and 01-stack-verification §3.8 measured Jupiter `tokens/v2/search` returning null `audit` and `stats5m` as thin as `['buyVolume','numBuys']` on sub-2-minute mints. So for coins aged 0-90s — the only coins the re-check is for — the designated fallback is the source that cannot see them. The single source that can is the PumpPortal create-stream, which appears nowhere in §B1's three queries. B4 also only models index *lag*; there is no state for the mint stream being *disconnected*, which makes `coin_index` silently blind to every mint since the drop while reporting fresh.
problems.fix: Make query 4 in §B1 a scan of the raw PumpPortal create-event ring buffer (last 15 min, in-memory, symbol_norm + pHash), and make it the primary source for the pre-sign re-check, with `coin_index` and Jupiter as corroboration only. Add `pipeline_health.mint_stream_connected_at`; when the stream has been down >60s, `.confirm-recheck` must read `We can't see brand-new coins right now — someone may have minted this in the last N minutes.` and stay non-blocking. Index freshness in minutes is the wrong health metric here; stream liveness is the right one.

problems.problem: ADOPTED STORIES WILL RENDER `Create coin` OVER A PERFECTLY BUYABLE COIN. The dataContract adds `match_state` with a CONFIRMED/UNSURE/REJECTED/ADOPTED enum, but every CTA in the spec reads `confirmed_count = count(match_state='CONFIRMED')`. §5.4 defines ADOPTED as 'pre-existing coin the story attached to → legit buy, weaker confidence, different UI', and §5.5 G5 keeps majors eligible as ADOPTED. So a story that legitimately attached to an existing coin has confirmed_count=0 and renders Create. B2 then compounds it: D-WEAK's worked example is `$PUMP already exists — a $1.8B token from 2024, unrelated to this story` with 'Primary stays Create $PUMP' — but §5.5 G5 says a story genuinely about Pump.fun *should* match $PUMP, as ADOPTED. The spec hard-codes Create for the exact case its own gate defines as a legitimate buy.
problems.fix: Define the CTA over a three-valued rollup, not a single count: `buy_count = count(match_state IN ('CONFIRMED','ADOPTED'))`. ADOPTED renders `Buy $TICKER` with the §5.4 'different UI' — a `.timing-pill` reading `existed before this story` rather than an earliness badge. D-WEAK must branch on `match_state`: ADOPTED for this story → primary becomes Buy; genuinely unrelated collision → primary stays Create, as written.

problems.problem: THE ANTI-DUPE CHECK IS DESIGNED ON AN API BUDGET THAT DOES NOT EXIST. §B1's 'live overlay: Jupiter tokens/v2/search' runs on form open, on every 250ms-debounced keystroke >=2ch, and on the pre-sign re-check. 01-stack-verification §3.8 measured keyless `tokens/v2/search` at 0.5 RPS — 200 on requests 1-4, 429 on 5-12 — and §1.8 notes `lite-api.jup.ag` is being throttled to zero. A 250ms debounce is up to 4 req/s from a single user typing one ticker. Keyed, it is 10 credits per call per §54. This design 429s on the first user.
problems.fix: Jupiter is not a per-keystroke surface. Per-keystroke checks hit `coin_index` and the local mint-stream buffer only (both local, sub-5ms). Jupiter fires exactly twice per session: once on form open, once on the pre-sign re-check, both server-side, both behind a 30s per-symbol cache shared across all users so a hot story's symbol costs one call for everyone. Add a token-bucket in front of it and specify the state when the bucket is empty: `.coll` gains `--dim` `Live check unavailable — checked against our index only.`

problems.problem: EVERY SDK SYMBOL IN §C1 IS UNVERIFIED, AND THE INSTRUCTION IS INCOMPLETE. `@pump-fun/pump-sdk` is not installed in this repo (`node_modules/@pump-fun` does not exist). 01-stack-verification §3.15 specifically warns that the 1.36.0 README documents fee-sharing symbols with full code samples that have zero occurrences in `dist/index.d.ts`, and names one function whose real name differs. §C1 uses `PUMP_FEES.createFeeSharingConfig` and `PUMP_FEES.updateFeeSharesV2` — neither the README's names nor verified against anything. Separately, `createV2Instruction({mint,name,symbol,uri,creator,user})` omits `is_mayhem_mode` and `is_cashback_enabled` (an `OptionBool` struct, not a bare bool), both of which are required instruction data per 02-refuted-claims, along with 16 accounts including four mandatory Mayhem PDAs even when mayhem is false. Mayhem mode is also an undecided product parameter that changes the coin's economics and is silently defaulted here — while `.safety-defaults` asserts supply and transfer-fee behaviour as constants.
problems.fix: Install the SDK and grep `dist/index.d.ts` before writing another line of §C1; treat every `PUMP_FEES.*` name as a placeholder until then. Add `is_mayhem_mode` and `is_cashback_enabled` to the instruction and make both explicit founder decisions in openQuestions — mayhem mode belongs next to D2, not defaulted in a code comment. Add `launch.mayhem_mode boolean` and `launch.cashback_enabled boolean`. Also note `toggle_create_v2(enabled)` is an authority-gated global switch pump.fun controls: the whole feature can be turned off upstream and the spec has no state for it.

problems.problem: THE FIRST-TIMER IS NOT TOLD THEY RECEIVE ZERO TOKENS, AND `.safety-defaults` ACTIVELY REINFORCES THE WRONG MODEL. 'The normie who saw something on TikTok' is one of three named users and appears nowhere in nine screens. The single most reliable first-timer misconception about launching on a bonding curve is that creating a coin means receiving the coins. `.safety-defaults` leads with `✓ Supply 1,000,000,000 — fixed, you can't mint more` — which a first-timer reads as 'I have a billion of these' — and the lime ✓ frames it as a benefit to them. With `.buychips` correctly defaulted to None, the modal first launch gives the creator a token balance of zero, and no screen in the flow says so. They will land on the success screen, click `Trade $CHILLGUY`, see a zero balance, and conclude they were robbed.
problems.fix: Add a row to `.safety-defaults`, first, in `--mono 11px` like the rest: `YOUR SUPPLY AT LAUNCH  0 — you buy at the same price as everyone else`. Add `Your $CHILLGUY` → `0` or `about 4,120,000` to `.confirm-rows` alongside `Your balance after`, so the number is stated at the moment of signing. On the success screen, when `first_buy_lamports = 0`, `.done-s` gains one `--muted` line: `You don't hold any $CHILLGUY. You earn from trading fees, not from supply.`

problems.problem: EARLINESS IS A STICKER, NOT A MECHANIC — AND THE ONE NUMBER RENDERED IS THE WRONG KIND OF NUMBER. Strip four decorative strings (`.sh-s` 'spotted 31 minutes early', `.lead-badge.sm +31m early`, `.done-s` '4 minutes after we spotted it', `.dupe-card` 'made 4m after the post') and this is pump.fun's create form with a duplicate check. Nothing in nine screens reads the two live earliness signals the pipeline already computes: `t_crypto = min(t_mint, t_ct)` from the PumpPortal websocket + ~300 CT accounts polled every 2 min, and the §3.4 lifecycle / acceleration state from the geometric snapshot grid. A creator deciding whether to spend $4 and 40 seconds needs 'is the window still open' and 'is this still accelerating'. Worse, the number that IS rendered is wrong in kind: §1 line 213 defines lead time over alerts 'where a coin appeared within 6h'. On the create path no coin exists by definition, so lead time is an OPEN interval that is still running — rendering it as a closed `+31m early` states a final figure for a measurement in progress.
problems.fix: Replace the static badge with the live one. `.src-quote` right rail becomes two mono cells: `SPOTTED  31m ago` and `CRYPTO TWITTER  not yet` (or `6m ago` once `t_ct` fires, in `--red`, with `.timing-pill.timing-late`). Add a third: `STORY  accelerating` / `cooling` / `peaked 11m ago`, from the §3.4 lifecycle field already being computed. Put the same three in `.confirm-rows`, re-read at step-2 mount, so the last thing before signing is whether the head start still exists. This is the only change that makes the create form unbuildable by a competitor without a detection pipeline.

problems.problem: D-IMAGE IS DESTROYED BY THE EXACT NUMBER A9 CITES TO JUSTIFY ITSELF. A9 reason 3 correctly cites §3.16: 58.6% of the newest 599 pump.fun coins have byte-identical logos, largest group 56 tokens from one creator. B1 query 2 then runs `bit_count(image_phash # $phash) <= 6` against `first_mint_at > now() - 7 days` — i.e. against 200k-300k mints drawn from exactly that 58.6%-duplicate corpus. Hamming <=6 on generic slop will match constantly. The D-IMAGE band as specified will fire on a large fraction of launches with a false `This image is already a coin`, and it fires hardest on the low-information images where it means least. The 10.0% figure §3.16 gives is for a liquidity-filtered corpus, which query 2 does not filter.
problems.fix: Gate D-IMAGE on image distinctiveness, using the IDF term §33 already hands you for free: suppress the band when `count(coin_index where image_sha256 = $sha) > 3` or when the matched group size exceeds 5, and require `liquidity_usd > 0` on the matched mint (§5.5 G4: filter before ranking, not after). Tighten to `<=4` for images whose SHA-256 group is non-singleton. Also flag the query cost: `bit_count(...)` is not indexable, so this is a filtered scan over ~250k rows on a latency-critical path — state the expected p95 or precompute a BK-tree.

problems.problem: THE DUPE-CARD'S PERSUASIVE FIELDS ARE PRECISELY THE ONES THAT ARE NULL IN THE MODAL CASE. The interstitial's entire argument is `$18.2K in it · 412 owners`. Its headline case is `$FERRY was made 40 seconds ago.` 01-stack-verification §3.8 measured `audit.topHoldersPercentage` null on 4 of 6 sub-2-minute mints and `stats5m` reduced to `['buyVolume','numBuys']`; the spec's own propagation section says a brand-new token renders all nine numeric cells as `—`. So the strongest push in the ladder degrades, in its commonest instance, to `$— in it · — owners`, which is a weaker argument than `Create it anyway` sitting next to it. No state covers this.
problems.fix: Add the state explicitly. When the duplicate is <90s old, the `.dupe-card` drops the money row entirely and leads with the only fact that is both available and decisive: `made 12 seconds after the post · nobody has traded it yet`, sourced from the mint stream, not Jupiter. Keep the primary as written for that band. Do not render `$0` or `$—` where a dollar figure was the argument — §5.3's rule that missing data fails closed applies to persuasion too.

problems.problem: STEP 1 HAS DRIFTED INTO A CONSUMER ONBOARDING FORM. The design language is 9-11px uppercase mono micro-labels, tabular figures and right-aligned numeric columns. Step 1 is a 560px sheet (every other sheet in the inventory is 472px; `.pd-sheet` is 440px), eight blocks at 15px gap, scrolling inside 72vh, containing roughly 100 words of running prose: the four-sentence `.split-poster` paragraph, `.split-note`, two `.disclaim` lines, `.buychips-note`, four `.safety-defaults` sentences, `.confirm-loss`. This is the only surface in Insidor written like a fintech onboarding flow, and it will read as a different product than the ranked table the user launched from. Step 2's `.confirm-rows` is a correct mono key/value table — the spec knows how, and did not do it in Step 1. The scroll makes it worse: the fee-split disclosure, the legally load-bearing block, is below the fold while the cost and primary are pinned.
problems.fix: Hold 472px. Convert `.safety-defaults` to a four-row mono key/value block with right-aligned values, matching `.confirm-rows`: `SUPPLY 1,000,000,000 · FIXED` / `YOUR SUPPLY 0` / `FREEZE NONE` / `TRANSFER FEE 0` / `LIQUIDITY SELF-SEEDED`. Convert `.split` to the `.split-bar` plus a three-row mono table (`YOU 5000 bps` / `@nordkyst_ferge 4000 bps` / `INSIDOR 1000 bps`), and move the four-sentence poster paragraph behind the same popover pattern the spec already invented for `.cost-pop`, triggered by the `hasn't claimed` pill. Move `.split` and `.disclaim` above `.buychips` so the disclosure is above the fold and the optional field is the thing that scrolls.

problems.problem: THE MISS IS STYLED DOWN RELATIVE TO THE HIT, AND THE SUBTITLE LIES ON NEGATIVE LEAD TIME. D2 requires misses to be as legible as hits. The spec renders a positive lead time as `.lead-badge.sm` — cyan, bordered, glowing — and a negative one as `.lead-dim`, which the component inventory defines as plain grey 10.5px mono. Same fact, two visual weights, the unflattering one quieter. Meanwhile `.sh-s` reads `from a story we spotted 31 minutes early` with no negative variant specified, so on a late detection it either renders a false claim or renders nothing with no fallback. The share card and `/c/{mint}` OG route compound it: they publish `Made 4 minutes after Insidor spotted this story` on a domain Insidor controls, and by construction only successes get shared — a hits-only public track record, which is the exact shape D2 exists to forbid.
problems.fix: Use the component that already exists for this: `.timing-pill.timing-late` (red, bordered, same weight as `.timing-early`) for negative lead time, not `.lead-dim`. Specify the `.sh-s` negative variant: `crypto Twitter got here 6 minutes before us`. Require `/c/{mint}` to render the story's signed lead time in the same treatment as the story page, including when negative, and to link to the public track record with its default 'All' filter. Also flag: §3.4 notes a merged post inherits `lead_time_min` from the merge target, so the number in `.src-quote` can be borrowed from a different story — render it only when `narratives.id` has not been through a merge since `promoted_at`, or mark it.

problems.problem: NAVIGATING TO A COIN PAGE DESTROYS THE FORM, AND THE DRAFT-RESUME STATE IS AN ORPHAN COLUMN. `.dupe-card` says 'Row click → coin page in a new context, preserving the form'; the interstitial's card says 'Tap → coin page'; `.dupe-unsure` offers `[View it]`. Interaction model §1.5 is unambiguous: there is one `#modalRoot`, every opener does `root.innerHTML=...`, and 'opening any modal destroys any modal already open' — and a route change destroys it outright. There is no 'new context' mechanism in this architecture and the spec never flags building one. Meanwhile the `launch` table carries `status text -- drafting|signing|...` and not one screen or state describes creating, resuming, or expiring a draft.
problems.fix: Pick one and specify it. Cheapest consistent with §1.5: coin pages from inside the create flow open in a new browser tab, exactly as the spec already does for `.src-quote`'s post permalink — one sentence, zero new machinery. If in-app navigation is wanted, then specify the draft: write `launch` with `status='drafting'` on form open, rehydrate on return, expire after 30 min, and add a 'resume a draft' state to the Step 1 state list. Do not ship a `drafting` enum value nothing writes.

problems.problem: NO LAUNCH RATE LIMIT, NO ABUSE STATE, AND THE INCENTIVE POINTS THE WRONG WAY. A7 caps model calls at 3 per user per story — the trivial cost — while nothing caps launches. One user can mint 40 coins off 40 stories in ten minutes. Under variant A each of those writes an unclaimed fee-share to a stranger's derived address and routes 10% to Insidor, so spam is directly monetised for the platform, which is the same incentive conflict openQuestions raises for D-STRONG but does not raise here, where it is larger. The spec also has no state for a user who has launched before — no history, no cooldown, no 'you launched 3 coins in the last hour' surface.
problems.fix: Add a per-user rate limit read server-side into `story_cta_v`: `launches_last_1h`, `launches_last_24h`. Above 3/hour the Create CTA renders with an `.achip`-styled cooldown label rather than disappearing, and Step 2 blocks with `You've launched 3 coins in the last hour. The next one unlocks in 14 minutes.` Add `launches_last_1h` to the honesty metrics alongside the create-anyway rate. Also add the `poster` guard: cap launches per unique poster handle per day, since 40 coins off one creator's posts is the case that produces a takedown.

problems.problem: THE NAMER'S LABEL LOOP ONLY LEARNS FROM SUCCESSES. A7 says 'every run writes namer_run{shown, accepted_symbol, accepted_edited}' and calls it 'a free, self-growing label set'. The `namer_run` schema has `accepted_symbol text -- null until submit`. Abandonment is the strongest negative signal the namer can generate — the name was bad enough that the user left — and it is indistinguishable from a row that simply has not been submitted yet. The A3 weight refit in build step 12 will therefore be fit on a hits-only sample, which is the D2 failure applied to the model instead of the track record.
problems.fix: Write `namer_run` at form open, not at submit, and add `outcome text -- accepted|edited|abandoned|typed_over` plus `time_to_first_keystroke_ms`. Set `abandoned` on sheet close without submit. Add the abandon rate next to `accepted_edited` in the >40% watch condition openQuestions already defines.

problems.problem: THE pg_trgm QUERY DOES NOT DO WHAT ITS COMMENT SAYS. B1 query 1: `where symbol_norm = $1 or symbol_norm % $1 -- pg_trgm, sim >= 0.6`. The `%` operator tests against the `pg_trgm.similarity_threshold` GUC, default 0.3, not against the value in the comment. As written this returns roughly double the intended candidate set on every keystroke, which then flows into a liquidity-ordered list the D-WEAK band renders as 'already exists'.
problems.fix: Either `set_limit(0.6)` per session, or drop `%` for the explicit predicate `similarity(symbol_norm, $1) >= 0.6` with the GIN index used via a separate `%` prefilter. State the chosen threshold as a tunable, since it directly controls the D-WEAK false-positive rate.

problems.problem: THE MINT KEYPAIR IS A SECOND SIGNER, WHICH THE 'ONE SIGNATURE' FRAMING HIDES. C1 generates `Keypair.generate()` for the mint and C3 persists it encrypted server-side, correctly, for retry safety. But pump.fun's `create_v2` requires the mint account to sign. The transaction therefore has two signers — the user's Privy wallet and the mint keypair — so the server must partially sign with the mint key and hand partially-signed bytes to Privy's raw-bytes API. The spec's 'two steps and one signature' framing and the `/api/launch/{prepare,sign,confirm}` split never mention it, and it materially changes what `prepare` returns.
problems.fix: State it: `/api/launch/prepare` returns a serialized transaction already partially signed by the mint keypair, with a blockhash and its expiry; `/api/launch/sign` accepts the user signature only. Keep 'one signature' as user-facing copy — it is true from the user's side — but make the server contract explicit, and note that the blockhash expiry clock starts at `prepare`, which interacts with the step-3 'blockhash expired' state.

problems.problem: INSIDOR'S CUT IS ABSENT FROM THE COST BREAKDOWN, AND THE SPLIT SWITCHES DENOMINATORS BETWEEN VARIANTS. The `.cost-pop` itemisation shows `pump.fun creation fee 0.0000 SOL — creation itself is free` and a `~0.0204 SOL` total, with no line for Insidor. A user reading the cost popover concludes Insidor charges nothing. Separately, variant A renders Insidor's share as a `10%` bar segment (share of the fee stream) while variant B's copy says `Insidor keeps 0.1%` (share of the trade) — the same fact in two denominators inside one component, which is the shape of a number being hidden even when it is not.
problems.fix: Add a final line to `.cost-pop`: `Insidor's cut  0.0000 SOL now — 10% of your fee stream (0.1% of each trade). See the split.` Pick one denominator for the bar labels and show both units in mono in every variant: `INSIDOR  1000 bps of fees · 0.1% of each trade`.

problems.problem: THE HAIKU COST FIGURE IS UNDERSTATED BY ROUGHLY 4x. A4 states '~900in/250out ≈ $0.0005'. That implies a blended rate near $0.43/MTok, which is below claude-haiku-4-5's input price alone. The number does not change any decision — the real constraint on the regeneration cap is the slot-machine dynamic, which openQuestions already identifies correctly — but it is a stated figure in a spec that is otherwise numerically careful, and it will be used to size a budget.
problems.fix: Re-derive against current published Haiku 4.5 rates and restate. Note the per-story cost is up to 3x this under the A7 cap, and that the attempt-1 result is cached on the story for 20 min, so the meaningful unit is cost-per-story, not cost-per-call.

problems.problem: `narratives.lead_time_min` IS LISTED AS 'EXISTS TODAY AND IS USED AS-IS' BUT ITS SEMANTICS ARE UNVERIFIED AGAINST THE PROSPECTIVE-CLOCK DEFINITION. §1 defines lead time as `t_crypto - promoted_at`, and the dataContract itself flags that `promoted_at` does not exist. So whatever today's `lead_time_min` is computed from, it is not the D2-honest number, yet the spec renders it directly in `.src-quote` and `.sh-s`. Relatedly, the migration backfills `promoted_at = coalesce(first_seen_at, created_at)` then freezes it — making `minutes_after_promote` on every pre-existing story a fabricated figure, and it is the success screen's headline number and the share card's public claim.
problems.fix: Do not render `lead_time_min` in the create sheet until it is recomputed from `promoted_at` against `t_crypto`. Add `narratives.promoted_at_backfilled boolean default false`, set true in the migration, and suppress both the `.done-s` earliness sentence and the share card's earliness line when it is true — fall back to `made from "Norwegian ferry horn"` with no minute figure. A fabricated screenshot number is the most expensive kind of dishonesty this product can ship.

missing: Two or more coins landing on the story while the form is open — the duplicate interstitial is single-coin by construction and this is the modal case on a hot story (§5.2 copycat swarms).

First-run user: never launched, no wallet, does not know what a ticker is. Named as one of three target users and absent from all nine screens. In particular there is no statement that the creator receives zero tokens at launch when the first buy is None.
